uncited: This family defines the specific algorithmic variations of the differentiable rasterization pipeline used to render 3D Gaussians, extending the standard alpha-compositing logic of [3D Gaussian Splatting Differentiable Rasterizer](2813-3d-gaussian-splatting-differentiable-rasterizer.md).
It addresses specialized requirements such as dynamic pruning gradients, X-ray physics, hybrid sigma fallbacks, and importance scoring, which the base rasterizer does not natively support.

All variants in this family operate on the same fundamental data structures: a set of 3D Gaussians defined by mean $\boldsymbol{\mu}$, covariance $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}$, opacity $\alpha$, and color/features.
They share the initial projection step, transforming 3D parameters to 2D screen space using extrinsic/intrinsic matrices and Jacobian transformations to compute 2D covariances.
They all utilize a tile-based sorting and accumulation strategy to ensure depth ordering and correct alpha blending.

The core divergence lies in how the alpha value $\alpha_i$ is computed, how the blending loop modifies the transmittance $T$ and color $C$, and what auxiliary data (masks, counts, or physics parameters) is propagated.
- **Definition**: A rasterization branch (`use_analytic_tau`) that computes the per-pixel accumulated analytic line-integral optical thickness $\tau$ along the view ray.
The base differentiable rasterizer for 3D Gaussian Splatting was introduced by Kerbl et al. in 2023.

The variants described here emerge from subsequent research into optimizing training dynamics (Masked-Rasterization, F-Count), extending the representation to non-visible spectra (DRR), and improving numerical stability or approximation accuracy (Hybrid Sigma, Analytic Tau).

detail: Alpha is derived physically as $\text{alpha} = 1 - \text{exp}(-\tau)$ using Beer-Lambert extinction, rather than using heuristic alpha values [S1, unofficial].
